# One-message WebSocket application

`sample_programs/library/websocket_once.lani` composes the generic upgrade and
stream modules with a real nonblocking TCP socket or verified TLS stream. The
Python fixture independently reads its HTTP request and masked client frames;
OpenSSL supplies TLS and certificate operations.

## Groups

| Group | Cases | Contract exercised |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `plain` | 9 | Upgrade and frame coalescing, empty stdin upload and empty response, binary/text messages, fragments, interleaved and late Ping/Pong, 126/65536-byte framing, first-message selection, masked Close exchange |
| `rejection` | 12 | Bad Accept, unoffered protocol, extensions, incomplete HTTP head, masked server frames, RSV, invalid UTF-8, early/abnormal Close, unclean EOF, unfinished fragmentation, oversized frame |
| `cli` | 17 | Help, argument validation, header/target injection rejection, numeric endpoint requirement, DNS TLS identity, duplicate options, input cap, no network on rejection |
| `io` | 3 | Actual closed stdout reader, stdin read failure, absolute deadline while awaiting Close; no premature stdout |
| `tls` | 5 | TLS 1.2/1.3 success, isolated default trust paths, DNS identity mismatch, untrusted CA; no application exchange before authentication |

The expected success output is exact binary message content. Every protocol or
trust failure must produce empty stdout. The peer verifies that client data,
Pong and Close frames are masked and decode to the required bytes. Separate
processes must supply fresh nonce values. No fixed production masking key or
test certificate is embedded in the program.

`controls` checks eight CPU-only properties of the independent wire oracle. It
does not execute Lanius and is never counted as a native application result.

## Reproduction

Compile the application with the repository compiler's native linker and both
`ssl` and `crypto` libraries, then run one group per command:

```sh
python3 -B tests/fixtures/extended/websocket_once/oracle.py controls
python3 -B tests/fixtures/extended/websocket_once/oracle.py plain PATH_TO_ELF
python3 -B tests/fixtures/extended/websocket_once/oracle.py rejection PATH_TO_ELF
python3 -B tests/fixtures/extended/websocket_once/oracle.py cli PATH_TO_ELF
python3 -B tests/fixtures/extended/websocket_once/oracle.py io PATH_TO_ELF
python3 -B tests/fixtures/extended/websocket_once/oracle.py tls PATH_TO_ELF
```

The runner has a 12-second per-process timeout and the Rust driver has an
80-second per-group bound. TLS certificates are ephemeral and generated by the
existing OpenSSL test helper. Traces in `cli` and the input-error case establish
network absence only; this suite makes no source-allocation, fd-leak,
allocation-failure, GPU-execution or formal-verification claim.

## Earlier failure and repair

The earlier source
`5055e3ed8cd0c0054db3f840e1cc9a2e0145189233161391b0ea25cb837f4391`
compiled and passed its plain/rejection/CLI/I/O groups, but its first TLS case
aborted with `free(): invalid pointer` (SIGABRT). Receipt:
`target/stdlib-work/websocket-once-tls-native-first.log`. Those earlier passes
were not used to accept the repaired source; all five groups ran again.

That source's transport enum matched an entire mutable TLS stream by value.
The repair stores borrowed socket/TLS references and keeps the actual owner in
lexical scope throughout exchange and cleanup. The same unchanged TLS oracle
then passed. The product repair changes the example's ownership boundary;
neither compiler code nor the test expectation changed.

The first compile stopped in an unannotated generic I/O result in the upgrade
module, matching the existing generic I/O inference dependency. Giving those
locals the declared trait result types advanced admission to an application
visibility error; adding `pub` to its two public-trait impl declarations made
the application compile. No compiler code changed.
